Note::TexAccessor::tabular_blocks¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::tabular_blocks() const

Extract Complete tabular/tabular* Environments¶

tabular_blocks() extracts every complete \begin{tabular}...\end{tabular} and \begin{tabular*}...\end{tabular*} region, including its delimiters, as one token per match, in source order. It is the tabular-family counterpart of tables: a table environment is the floating wrapper, while tabular is the actual row/column content, and the two often appear nested — a tabular block inside a table environment is still extracted on its own, independent of the surrounding table.

Both the starred and unstarred forms are recognized in the same pass and interleaved in document order. A similarly named but distinct environment — array, in particular — is not recognized; only the two exact names above match. An unterminated \begin{tabular}broken with no closing tag is dropped rather than partially returned.

The closed TokenBatch stores every extracted region — delimiters included — in its rank-1 Text tokens() Note. Its Int64 offsets() has source.numel() + 1 entries, so flattened source cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). The receiver is not mutated.

Undefined yields undefined tokens with offsets [0]. Empty cells and cells without a tabular environment produce empty intervals. Only Text is accepted.

Example 1: Starred, Unstarred, Nested-In-table, And A Look-Alike Environment¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\begin{tabular*}wide\end{tabular*} x \begin{tabular}plain\end{tabular})",
    R"(\begin{table}\begin{tabular}inside\end{tabular}\end{table})",
    R"(\begin{array}not tabular\end{array} \begin{tabular}broken)"});
const auto blocks = source.tex().tabular_blocks();

std::cout << blocks.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\begin{tabular*}wide\\end{tabular*}", "\\begin{tabular}plain\\end{tabular}", "\\begin{tabular}inside\\end{tabular}"]

Cell 0 contributes both the starred and unstarred region. Cell 1’s tabular block is extracted on its own, independent of the surrounding table wrapper — no \begin{table} markers appear in the token. Cell 2 contributes nothing: array is a different environment name, and \begin{tabular}broken has no closing tag.

Example 2: Per-Cell Offsets¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = blocks.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 3, 3]

Cell 0 owns two tokens, cell 1 owns its one nested block, and cell 2 owns none.

Example 3: No Tabular Content Anywhere¶

const auto empty_batch = pluss::make_note({"plain", ""}).tex().tabular_blocks();
std::cout << empty_batch.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().tabular_blocks().tokens().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().tabular_blocks();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "tabular blocks Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
tabular blocks Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • tables: the floating environment tabular content commonly appears inside.

  • env("tabular"): a single exact form, without the starred variant.
